output_text: {"hypothesis":"The drop is most likely caused by the train and test paths encoding features differently, not by the missing indicator itself. pandas.read_csv turns stalk_root='' into NaN in train. The test_rows dicts keep it as the empty string ''. As a result, the missing indicator is 1 in train but 0 in test, and '' becomes an unseen category. A second likely cause is that category or label codes are built separately for train and test, for example by calling astype('category') or LabelEncoder on each side. If so, the same letter maps to different integer codes. Either way the model ranks test rows on misaligned features.","rationale":"raw ROC AUC is 0.7426, well below baseline_raw 0.8502. The normalized dev score of -0.91 matches that. correct=true, cheat_flags is empty, and there is no runtime error, so the output format is valid and this is genuine bad ranking, not a crashed grader. The task has only 4 low-cardinality categorical predictors and about 5k rows. LightGBM is unlikely to fall more than 0.1 AUC below baseline on that alone; ordinary model differences do not explain a drop that large. A drop that large usually means feature semantics differ between training and inference. The visible sample shows stalk_root missing in a large share of rows, and those rows correlate strongly with the label, for example k,e,,p,1 and k,w,,g,0. That makes the NaN vs '' mismatch especially damaging. There is no sign of a suspicious score jump or leakage.","advice":"1) Unify the reading path. Read train.csv with dtype=str and keep_default_na=False, or replace NaN with an explicit 'MISSING' token right after reading. In test, map '' to the same 'MISSING' token. Compute the missing indicator from that one rule on both sides. 2) Fix the category mapping. Learn the category list or encoder from train only. Apply it to test with the same categories, for example pd.Categorical(test_col, categories=train_categories), and map unseen values to one fallback level. Do not build codes independently on test. Keep the test column order identical to train. 3) Self-check without the grader. Do K-fold on train.csv only. Turn each validation fold into a list[dict[str,str]] with missing values as '', and score it through the full fit_predict entry point. Compare that AUC with an internal DataFrame-only evaluation. If the two differ a lot, the inference path is confirmed as the bug. 4) Use a robustness comparison. With only 4 categorical columns, try either smoothed target encoding over the full combination of the 4 features with backoff to lower-order combinations, or one-hot plus pairwise interaction logistic regression. Compare its CV AUC with LightGBM. For LightGBM, use native categorical_feature or one-hot, keep min_data_in_leaf moderate, and do not treat label-encoded integers as continuous. 5) Finally, assert that the output length equals len(test_rows), the order is preserved, and every value is finite and in [0,1]."}
